items.title: Remove Dead Code from Next Server
items.body:
This removes dead code from `next-server`.

We had references to `amphtml` and `hasAmp`—these values are not used anywhere else in the code base.

items.title: Fix RenderOpts in `next-server`
items.body:
This pull request correctly types the `RenderOpts` arguments in `next-server`.

As a side effect, it caught a couple situations:

- `previewProps` were not passed in all scenarios (assign in shared object instead of on individual call sites)
- `isDataReq` was of the wrong type (added `!!` to booleanify)
- Revealed we're sharing the object for `pageData` and `sprRevalidate` (added TODOs to fix)

I've added a test to ensure this does not regress. I also fixed a double cookie setting issue identified as a result of this new test.

items.title: Add example for polyfilling DOMParser in Node
items.body:
This pull request addresses #10533 and updates the `with-react-intl` example to show the user how they can enable support for `FormattedHTMLMessage` on the server by polyfilling `DOMParser`.

I have disabled the polyfill by default since the dependency on `xmldom` (or `jsdom`) might be a little heavy if you are not using `FormattedHTMLMessage` (which is a legacy feature and not recommended anyway). Though, this dependency is only included on the server so that might be not as big of an issue. What do you think?

Fixes #10533

items.title: Throw NoFallbackError instead of returning
items.body: The `false` variation can't cleanly be modeled in a `(req, res) => Promise<void>` universe, so lets change it to throw an error for now. We can probably remove this in the future.

items.title: Allows multiple lines for `Module not found` errors
items.body:
Next is currently removing useful information from the PnP error messages.

Before:

```
Module not found: Something that got detected as your top-level application (because it doesn't seem to belong to any package) tried to access a package that is not declared in your dependencies
```

After:

```
Module not found: Something that got detected as your top-level application (because it doesn't seem to belong to any package) tried to access a package that is not declared in your dependencies

Required package: foo (via "foo/components/Avatar")
Required by: /home/arcanis/foo/bar.tsx
```

items.title: Generic form of GetStaticProps and GetServerSideProps
items.body:

```ts
type MyProps = { slug: string };
export default (props: MyProps) => ...
export const getStaticProps: GetStaticProps<MyProps> = async (ctx) => ... 
```

items.title: Fix getStaticPaths example code
items.body:
In the upcoming `getStaticPaths` documentation, there seems to be a contradiction in what should be returned by this function.

In one place, it says it should look something like this:
```js
return {
  paths: [
    { params: { id: 1 } },
    { params: { id: 2 } }
  ],
  fallback: ...
}
```

So `paths` contains a list of objects, where each item has a `params` property, that are objects themselves.

Although, in the example below [`fallback`](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/canary/docs/basic-features/data-fetching.md#the-fallback-key-required), `paths` was equal to posts mapped over to a list of strings (ids).

Closes #10894

items.title: docs(examples): add with-iron-session example

labels.name: examples
labels.description: Issue was opened via the examples template.

items.body:
This example creates an authentication system that uses a **signed and encrypted cookie to store session data**. It relies on [`next-iron-session`](https://github.com/vvo/next-iron-session).

It uses current best practices as for authentication in the Next.js ecosystem:
1. **no `getInitialProps`** to ensure every page is static
2. **`useUser` hook** together with [`swr`](https://swr.now.sh/) for data fetching

**Features:**
- Logged in status synchronized between browser windows/tabs
- Layout based on logged in status
- All pages are static
- Session data is signed and encrypted in a cookie

cc @lfades this is inspired by https://github.com/zeit/next.js/pull/10529/files
cc @timneutkens this follows your comment here: https://github.com/zeit/next.js/discussions/10724#discussioncomment-726

Areas for improvements:
- ux: loading shell just like https://zeit.co/dashboard/abcdefgh
- ~security: should we restrict important routes to POST? There's no "security" documentation in Next.js website and that worries me. For example /logout is subject to csrf because one could send a link to /logout and it would log me out even if the cookie is secure, httpOnly and SameSite lax~ there's no issue in this PR about security. But in general if you use Next.js you should make sure to do sensitive work via non GET requests (like no GET /user/delete) otherwise you'd have security issues (people could send you to pages that would destroy data)
- ~logout: right now this is a simple a href link to /api/logout, can we do it differently?~ implemented async logout using swr mutate

**Demo**:
![2020-03-11 16 04 04](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/123822/76431563-07897980-63b2-11ea-9669-8fc19130fd0b.gif)

items.title: Correct Cache-Control Behavior for GS(S)P
items.body:
This pull request:

- Extracts `sendPayload` as a helper (similar to `sendHTML` (legacy for `getInitialProps`))
- Updates `next-serverless-loader` to use `sendPayload`, removing duplicated logic
- Updates `sendPayload`'s `options` object to be more strictly typed
- Only sets `Cache-Control` header if not already set for `getServerSideProps` (still forced for `getStaticProps` and Preview Mode)
- Updates tests accordingly

This adjusts the default `getServerSideProps` `Cache-Control` header from `no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` to `private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate` (adds `private` and `max-age=0`).

---

Closes #10993

labels.name: examples
labels.description: Issue was opened via the examples template.

items.body:
The current examples are using `getServerSideProps` with API Routes, which has the following downsides:
- The ZEIT Now deployment doesn't work because it uses an absolute URL to localhost. (And relative URLs only work for the browser)
- It adds SSR to an use case where it's not required

Client side data fetching fixes the above issues, the use case could still be better for SSG, but the idea of this examples is to show the usage of API Routes. We could change them in the future to do actions instead of data loading, but for the moment this is a good fix.

items.title: Fix bug where pages refresh periodically for custom server
items.body: Fixes #11243.  When rendering a page where the path name doesn't start with a `/` with a custom server the page will refresh every 5 seconds. This is due to the fact that the `entries` object in the `onDemandEntryHandler` checks for keys that start with a `/`, and when the page is rendered without a `/` the entry can't be properly found. The solution fo this was to add an error when a user attempts to render a page that doesn't start witha `/`.

items.title: Use Lax Cookie for Preview Mode
items.body:
We currently use `Strict` SameSite cookies for Preview Mode. The reason for this pick was arbitrary, as we were erring to the least privileged option.

This pull request updates our Preview Mode cookie behavior to be `Lax`, which allows the following workflows:

- Embedded previews within CMSes (using an `<iframe>`)
- Redirects from Email or CMS authorization flow(s) will not require a page refresh to make "same origin"

We are comfortable with `Lax` as Chrome is moving to make this the default option for all cookies:
https://chromestatus.com/feature/5088147346030592

Using a `Lax` cookie is more secure than most browsers' current default: no same site requirement (`Lax` is more secure than browsers' current default: `None`).

---

Fixes #10881
